takeaway: Today and Monday stay hot, sunny and gusty, around 34°C in Nicoya, with offshore winds in the mornings and a solid southwest swell (6–9 ft at 16 seconds). Then the weather turns: the U.S. marine forecasters now flag a low that may form southwest of Costa Rica late Tuesday, bringing strong southwest winds and rough seas offshore through Thursday night. Expect a wet, onshore stretch Tuesday Nov 3 through Friday Nov 6, heaviest Wednesday and Thursday. The prolonged-rain watch moves up to elevated. No hurricane-center storm threat to Costa Rica.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Sun Nov 1 – Tue Nov 3)
periods.pattern: Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) has few clouds and wind on the North Pacific this morning, partly cloudy with gusts this afternoon, and partly cloudy tonight. Nicoya's high is about 34°C with a low near 22°C, and Liberia about 35°C. IMN issued a notice Saturday for moderate to strong trade winds this weekend, which bring rain to the Caribbean side, not to us. The models keep Nosara at about 1–3 mm today and about 4–6 mm Monday. Tuesday the trades fade, a weak tropical wave passes, and the shower belt moves north: every model average puts about 16–22 mm (two-thirds of an inch to just under an inch) at Nosara on Tuesday.
periods.implications: Today and Monday are good outdoor days, best in the morning. It's hot, windy and dusty. Tuesday turns showery, mostly in the afternoon and evening, so get errands and outdoor plans done by Monday.
periods.confidence: High on today and Monday staying mostly dry. Moderate to high on Tuesday afternoon showers.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Wed Nov 4 – Sat Nov 7)
periods.pattern: This is the wet core. The U.S. marine forecast says a low may develop southwest of Costa Rica late Tuesday and push strong southwest winds and rough seas into the waters off Costa Rica and Panama into early Friday. The models agree on Pacific-side rain fed by southwest winds. At Nosara, the American average shows about 57 mm (over 2 inches) on Wednesday, then about 16 mm a day Thursday and Friday. The European average shows about 35 mm on both Wednesday and Thursday and about 16 mm Friday and Saturday. The European AI average and the regular American run are lighter, about 16–22 mm Wednesday and under 10 mm by Friday. The regular European run is the wettest, with about 48 mm Wednesday and about 70 mm (nearly 3 inches) Thursday. The heaviest rain in most maps sits just offshore to the southwest, so totals at Nosara could swing a lot either way.
periods.implications: Plan for a rainy stretch. Expect downpours with thunder, and on Wednesday or Thursday a real chance of a longer, steadier soaking rather than one afternoon storm. Watch for flooded dirt roads, fast-rising creeks and river crossings, and avoid driving at night in heavy rain. Saturday should start to improve.
periods.confidence: High on Wednesday through Friday being wet. Moderate on how heavy. Low on exact amounts, since the models range from about 16 mm to 70 mm on the wettest day.

periods.label: Days 8–15 (Sun Nov 8 – Sun Nov 15)
periods.pattern: The low moves away and the trade winds return over Nicaragua and Guanacaste around Nov 8–10, strong again by about Nov 11. Model averages drop to about 1–4 mm a day from Nov 9 through Nov 15. IMN's long-range outlook (issued Oct 26) still calls for drier than normal weather through Nov 22, with the dry season settling in on the North Pacific.
periods.implications: Expect a clear dry-out. Plans from about Nov 9 onward look like the safest bet, with sunny, breezy days returning.
periods.confidence: Moderate to high on drying out from about Nov 9. Low on any stray late shower.

surfWinds.regime: Caribbean trades, so it's offshore at Nosara this morning and Monday morning. The trades fade Tuesday, go southeast Tuesday night, and turn onshore from the southwest on Wednesday. Wednesday through Friday is a Pacific onshore pattern with choppy faces.
surfWinds.detail: The Papagayo marine forecast (issued 2:02 a.m. Pacific time, 4:02 a.m. Costa Rica time) has northeast to east winds of 20–25 knots out in the Gulf of Papagayo today and 15–20 knots elsewhere, with 6–9 ft of southwest swell at 16 seconds. Tonight and Monday are northeast 15–20 knots with 6–8 ft at 15 seconds. Monday night eases to east 10–15, Tuesday east 10–15 with 4–6 ft at 14 seconds, and Tuesday night southeast 10–15. Wednesday flips to southwest 10–15 knots with a new 6–8 ft south to southwest swell at 13 seconds, then light and variable in the gulf and west around 10 knots elsewhere through Thursday. Just south of the peninsula it's already west around 10 knots today, and it builds to southwest and west 15–20 knots Tuesday night through Wednesday night with seas 6–9 ft, so Nosara sits on the edge and afternoons there go side-on or onshore sooner than spots farther north. The forecast also flags isolated storms offshore this afternoon and scattered showers and storms tonight through Monday night. Nicaragua looks offshore all day today and Monday, a good sign for clean Nosara mornings, but that doesn't mean Nosara holds offshore all day.
surfWinds.bestWindows: This morning and Monday morning at first light, with the biggest, longest-period swell and offshore wind. It will be windy, so go early before it gets bumpy. Long-period sets come bigger and less often than the average suggests, and rip currents run stronger. Tuesday morning is likely the last clean session. Wednesday through Friday expect onshore, choppy and stormy conditions with a short-period swell. Clean offshore mornings should return around Nov 9–11 with the trades.
surfWinds.confidence: High on offshore mornings today and Monday. Moderate to high on onshore southwest winds from Wednesday. Moderate on how strong they get at Nosara itself.

gyreWatch.status: Elevated, up from a moderate watch. Not established. The U.S. marine forecasters now mention a possible low southwest of Costa Rica with strong southwest winds, the classic setup for a temporal, but it's not locked in.
gyreWatch.possibleTiming: Late Tuesday Nov 3 through Friday Nov 6, heaviest Wednesday and Thursday, easing Saturday Nov 7.
gyreWatch.supporting: The marine forecast synopsis says a low may develop southwest of the Costa Rica offshore waters late Tuesday with strong southwest winds and seas to 9 ft into early Friday. All the model averages and runs show southwest to west winds south of Costa Rica Tuesday through Friday and a wide area of heavy rain just southwest of Nicoya. The American average jumped to about 57 mm at Nosara on Wednesday, and the regular European run shows about 48 mm Wednesday and 70 mm Thursday with a weak low-pressure area near Nicoya by Thursday night. IMN expects a weak tropical wave early in the week, and NOAA's tropics outlook (Oct 27) notes a window for a late-season East Pacific storm in the Nov 4–17 period.
gyreWatch.conflicting: No model average shows a strong or slow-spinning low parked over Costa Rica, and the heaviest rain mostly stays offshore. The European AI average and the regular American run are much lighter. The trades return over Nicaragua by about Nov 8–10, so the spell looks to last three to four days, not a week or more. IMN's long-range outlook still expects drier than normal weather through Nov 22, and IMN's notices so far are about trade winds, not Pacific rain. The hurricane center expects nothing near Central America; its only East Pacific area is far southeast of Hawaii (now 50% in 7 days), and nothing is expected in the Caribbean.

whatChanged: The marine forecasters now mention a possible low forming southwest of Costa Rica late Tuesday, with strong southwest winds and rough seas into early Friday, which moves the prolonged-rain watch up to elevated. The wettest day in the American average is now Wednesday at about 57 mm (up from about 48 mm), and the regular European run is much wetter, around 70 mm Thursday. The switch to onshore southwest winds came forward to Wednesday morning (was Wednesday night). This morning's trades are a bit stronger in the Gulf of Papagayo (20–25 knots), and IMN issued a notice Saturday about strong trade winds this weekend. The dry-out now looks a day or so later, around Nov 8–9. The hurricane center's area far southeast of Hawaii rose to 50%.
practical: Surf at first light today and Monday for the biggest swell with offshore wind, and watch for strong rip currents. Do outdoor plans, shopping and errands by Monday. Tuesday afternoon turns showery, and Wednesday through Friday (Nov 4–6) looks genuinely wet, with a chance of a long soaking: be careful on dirt roads and at river crossings, and secure anything that could be damaged by heavy rain. Expect it to dry out from about Nov 8–9. No hurricane threat to Costa Rica.
alerts: IMN notice (Oct 31): moderate to strong trade winds this weekend, with rain on the Caribbean side and the Northern Zone.
